statement: In an isosceles triangle, the angle between the two equal sides is $3$ times as large as each of the other two angles. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle between the two equal sides?

choices.misconception: I found the two equal angles, 36 degrees each, and gave one of those instead of the angle between the equal sides.
I wrote 3x + x = 180, counting only one of the two equal angles, so I got x = 45 and gave that.
I found that each of the other two angles is 36 degrees, then doubled it instead of tripling it.
I wrote 3x + x = 180, forgetting that there are two equal angles, so x = 45 and 3x = 135.

hints: In an isosceles triangle, the two angles that are not between the equal sides are equal to each other.
Call each of those two angles $x^\circ$. The third angle is $3x^\circ$, and all three add up to $180^\circ$.

solutions.reliable: The two angles opposite the equal sides are equal; call each of them $x^\circ$. The angle between the equal sides is $3x^\circ$. The angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$, so $x + x + 3x = 5x = 180$, which gives $x = 36$. The angle between the equal sides is $3 \cdot 36^\circ = 108^\circ$. Check: $36 + 36 + 108 = 180$.
solutions.elegant: The three angles are in the ratio $1 : 1 : 3$, so the largest is $\frac{3}{5}$ of $180^\circ$, which is $108^\circ$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
